chunk_text: Pillai College of Engineering follows the curriculum provided by the University of Mumbai. The curriculum planning and delivery are diligent with the preparation of the lesson plan, adapting Bloom's Taxonomy focusing on Information, Understanding, Application, and Synthesis. Academic calendar is prepared and lesson plans are reviewed by HODs. Teachers maintain course files documenting all details of lectures, attendance, and internal marks.

The Nature Club of Pillai College of Engineering organizes annual cleanliness drives, tree plantations, and rallies to create awareness about cleanliness and environmental issues. In addition, subjects like Business Communication and Ethics, Intellectual Property Rights, and Cyber Security address professional ethics. Women Development Cell (WDC) renamed as Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) handles safety, security, and gender sensitization workshops.

PCE assesses the learning levels of students after admission. Slow learners are identified based on their performance in the first internal assessment test. Extra lectures, remedial classes, and study camps are conducted for slow learners to help them pass examinations. Advanced learners are mentored to take up complex projects, participate in hackathons (like AICTE Smart India Hackathon), and are supported to prepare for GATE, GRE, TOEFL, and CAT exams.

PCE has a dedicated mentor-mentee scheme where a small group of students (approx 15-20) is allotted to a faculty mentor. The mentors monitor academic progress, attendance, and address stress-related or personal issues of students. Periodic parent-teacher meetings (PTM) are organized to discuss student progress. An in-house counsellor is also available to resolve stress-related concerns.

PCE utilizes student-centric methods like project-based learning (PBL) from the first year itself. Every semester, students complete projects crossing multiple subjects. The college has a Maker Studio with 3D printers, laser cutters, and CNC machines for prototyping. Students also access a Component Library to borrow electronic sensors, microcontrollers, and actuators for their projects.

The Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) established in 2017 conducts annual Academic and Administrative Audits (AAA) to review teaching-learning processes. The IQAC pioneered project-based learning and set up the Component Library. The Academic Monitoring System (AMS) tracks attendance, daily lecture entry, and syllabus coverage dynamically.
